theory.intro: A length can be written in two ways: as a whole number of small units, or as a decimal of larger units. For example $165$ cm $= 1.65$ m.
facts: There are $100$ cm in $1$ m, so each centimetre is $\tfrac{1}{100}$ of a metre ($0.01$ m).
There are $1000$ mm in $1$ m and $10$ mm in $1$ cm.
Place value carries the meaning: $1.65$ m is $1$ whole metre and $65$ hundredths of a metre.
steps: Decide which units are used and how many smaller units make one larger unit: $100$ cm $=1$ m, $1000$ mm $=1$ m, or $10$ mm $=1$ cm.
When converting to smaller units, multiply by the conversion factor. When converting to larger units, divide by the conversion factor.
Use decimal place value to check the result. In metres, hundredths are centimetres and thousandths are millimetres; in centimetres, tenths are millimetres. Keep zeros in empty places.

workedExamples.question_text:
Record each length using decimal notation.
(a) $283$ cm in metres
(b) $76$ mm in centimetres
(c) $13$ mm in metres
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $283\text{ cm}=2\text{ m }83\text{ cm}$.
$83\text{ cm}$ is $83$ hundredths of a metre.
$283\text{ cm}=2.83\text{ m}$.
(b) $76\text{ mm}=7\text{ cm }6\text{ mm}$.
$6\text{ mm}$ is $6$ tenths of a centimetre.
$76\text{ mm}=7.6\text{ cm}$.
(c) $13\text{ mm}$ is $13$ thousandths of a metre.
Write the thousandths using three digits: $013$.
$13\text{ mm}=0.013\text{ m}$.

workedExamples.question_text:
Convert these lengths to the stated units.
(a) $4.036$ m in millimetres
(b) $8.7$ cm in millimetres
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Millimetres are smaller than metres, so multiply by $1000$.
$4.036\times1000=4036$.
$4.036\text{ m}=4036\text{ mm}$.
(b) Millimetres are smaller than centimetres, so multiply by $10$.
$8.7\times10=87$.
$8.7\text{ cm}=87\text{ mm}$.

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) Express $5$ m $+7$ cm in metres.
(b) Convert $4089$ mm to metres.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $7\text{ cm}=0.07\text{ m}$, because centimetres are hundredths of a metre.
$5\text{ m}+7\text{ cm}=5\text{ m}+0.07\text{ m}=5.07\text{ m}$.
(b) Metres are larger than millimetres, so divide by $1000$.
$4089\div1000=4.089$.
$4089\text{ mm}=4.089\text{ m}$.

foundation.question_text: Record $142$ cm as a decimal number of metres.

foundation.solution_text:
Convert to smaller units, so multiply by $100$.
$2.46\times100=246$.
$2.46\text{ m}=246\text{ cm}$.

foundation.question_text: Record $68$ mm as a decimal number of centimetres.

foundation.solution_text:
Convert to smaller units, so multiply by $10$.
$12.8\times10=128$.
$12.8\text{ cm}=128\text{ mm}$.
